title: Fold a camera's vari-angle screen shut with its glass facing the body
instruction: Leave the camera's rear screen folded flush against the body with its glass facing inward.
context: Done by camera rental check-in technicians and repair counter staff, who close vari-angle screens glass-in before casing a camera so the glass is not scratched. The fold is ordered on two axes and its direction depends on the start: the swivel is blocked unless the screen is swung out, the screen folds only when square, and folding straight back leaves the glass out. Unlike TK-KGYJKJ (earcups turned on fold and swivel hinges), the turn here must be read from how the camera stands.
setup: World frame: x away from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; heights above the table top. One loose mirrorless camera, 0.65 kg, standing on its base; in lot A its lens points away from the robot and its grip is on the robot's right. Body: black plastic box 40 mm deep (x) x 116 mm wide x 70 mm tall, with a viewfinder hump 36 x 50 x 18 mm on top (88 mm tall in all), a grip 20 x 26 x 66 mm in front at its right end, a kit lens 62 mm across and 50 mm long (front ring 56 mm across), centred 38 mm up and 5 mm to the camera's left of the body's centre. In lot A the body's back face is at x 360 mm, spanning y -18 to +98 mm. Screen: 75 x 55 x 13 mm, 40 g, black glass on one face and a silver back on the other, on a two-axis vari-angle mount: a vertical side hinge 7.5 mm behind the back face at y 96 mm, 35.5 mm up, swinging 0 (folded on the back) to a stop at 175 degrees (swung out to the robot's left), and a swivel about the screen's width through its middle, from -90 to +180 degrees (stops). Both hinges are friction hinges that stay where they are left. Folded at swivel 0 the glass faces out (shooting position); at 180 it faces the body. Start, both lots: the screen swung out to its 175-degree stop and lying flat 35.5 mm up beside the camera's left side, glass up. Lot A (the screenshot): as above, the screen at y about 107 to 182 mm. Lot B: the camera turned round (lens toward the robot), its back face at x 380 mm facing away from the robot, its body spanning y -98 to +18 mm, so the screen lies on the robot's right (y about -182 to -107 mm). Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial, after the robot has let go (no part of either arm, fingers to shoulder, within 5 mm of the camera or its screen) and with the screen still for 1 s. 1.0: the screen is folded flush on the camera's back (side hinge within 3 degrees of shut) with its glass facing the body (swivel within 8 degrees of its 180-degree stop). 0.5: the screen is turned glass-toward-the-body (swivel within 8 degrees of its 180-degree stop) but not folded flush. 0: anything else, for example folded with the glass facing out, turned the wrong way, left flat, still held, or the camera tipped more than 5 degrees or lifted more than 3 mm off the table. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: 1. Lot A: stand the camera on the table, lens pointing away from the robot, its back face 360 mm out from the arm bases and its centre 40 mm to the robot's left of the midline. Lot B: lens pointing toward the robot, its back face 380 mm out and its centre 40 mm to the robot's right. 2. Swing the screen out on its side hinge to its 175-degree stop. 3. Turn it on its swivel until it lies flat with the glass up. 4. Run with -E object_jitter=0; trial k uses lot A for even k and lot B for odd k.
fidelity: Built from boxes and cylinders at true size. The housing's interference is enforced through the hinges' limits: the swivel turns only when swung out at least 75 degrees, and the screen folds past 75 degrees only when square (within 8 degrees of 0 or 180). Friction hinges are springs whose rest point follows the joint (slip at 0.034 and 0.011 N m); the side hinge clicks shut within 4 degrees. Two lots (the camera turned round) stop a single fixed habit, not a memorised replay of both.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B); demo: 1.0 in each lot
